Thanks for the quick sync today — great conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned before we ship the pilot scope doc:

Call summary (what we heard)
- Primary workload: chat + streaming for short user prompts (median token output ~40 tokens).
- Expected steady-state conversation rate: 60–120 QPS across peaks, with short bursts up to ~250 QPS for 2–3 minutes.
- Latency target: p95 generation (end-to-end) <= 200ms for non-streamed single-turn responses; streaming handshake and first-byte p50 <= 120ms.
- Concurrency per-session: ~4–6 concurrent streams per user on average; global concurrency target ~1,200 active sessions during peak.
- Availability/SLO ask: 99.9% monthly.

Immediate questions we need to lock down before sizing the Dedicated pool:
1) Payload characteristics — confirmation of prompt sizes (average prompt tokens + embedding calls per request). You mentioned 12–14 tokens avg input and 2 embedding calls per unique user session — please confirm.
2) Percent of requests that actually stream vs batch-only (you estimated ~70% streaming).
3) Acceptable fallback behavior if a model variant is out of capacity (auto-failover to a slightly higher-latency model vs queueing).

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
- Cetera: confirm payload stats and streaming ratio — Alex (by EOD Thu 12/9).
- Redwood: produce a pilot sizing spreadsheet with GPU candidate matrix, reserved throughput windows, and estimated cost-band for a 4-week pilot — Chloe & Ben (deliver by Fri 12/11).
- Technical kickoff for pilot bench: 30–45 min sync to confirm test harness & metrics (tentative Mon 12/14) — Karthik to lead.

Attachments: I’ll attach an initial sizing template and a short GPU tradeoff snapshot so you can see the levers we’ll use. If anything below is off, call it out and I’ll update.

Best,
Chloe

Thanks Chloe — quick technical notes from our end after the call:

1) GPU candidates and the tradeoffs we’ll run in the pilot (high level) - A100 80GB (FP16 / q4f16): best single-request latency for larger context, higher cost per-hour, best for bursty latencies. - H100 80GB (FP16 / q4f16): slightly lower latency for attention-heavy models at high concurrency; newer kernel optimizations for streaming. - L40s / RTX 6000-class (q4_0/q4_1): lower cost options, decent throughput for small-context streaming but higher p95 under concurrency.

2) Reserve throughput & headroom assumptions - For the stated p95 <= 200ms target (end-to-end), with median 40-token output and ~14-token input, our back-of-the-envelope indicates ~6–8 tokens/ms on H100 for the model family you mentioned (decoder-only open model family). - To support sustained 120 QPS with 40-token generation target under that latency, the Dedicated pool should reserve roughly 8–10 x H100-equivalent devices (we’ll quantify precisely in the spreadsheet). For peak bursts to 250 QPS, we suggest burst capacity via the hosted spare pool or autoscaling policy to avoid queueing.

3) Streaming-specific considerations
- Warm KV cache per session matters: if sessions re-use context, effective per-token time drops significantly. We’ll need a realistic session-locality metric (fraction of requests that reuse same conversation). - For streaming-first-byte p50 <= 120ms, we recommend an initial handshake path pinned to low-latency instance types (H100 preferred) for the pilot.

Questions for Cetera (to confirm sizing)
- Can you share distribution of session-locality (e.g., % of requests that repeat within 2 minutes vs cold starts)?
- Any hard deadline on pilot results (e.g., procurement windows)?

I’ll pull a quick GPU-cost delta table and drop it in the sizing sheet Chloe referenced. Happy to jump on the technical kickoff with Karthik.

-Ben

Thanks Chloe and Ben — useful recap. Quick answers:

- Payload: average prompt length ~13 tokens; we do 1 embedding call per new session and then incremental embedding updates ~10% of the time.
- Streaming share: you’re right — about 65–70% of requests stream on production traffic.
- Session-locality: roughly 45% of requests are warm within a 5-minute window; the rest are cold.
- Pilot timing: procurement wants a 4-week bench that starts before end of Q1 — ideally kickoff in late January, but we can run a short validation test earlier if Redwood needs earlier telemetry.

On fallback: for the pilot we prefer an auto-failover to a slightly higher-latency model (same family) rather than queueing users; we’ll accept a small quality delta as long as latency remains bounded.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you include a short cost envelope for a 4-week pilot (low/med/high) tied to the GPU candidates?
2) Please forward your SOC2/infosec intake so we can start the procurement thread.
